Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class UriTemplate

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.UriTemplate
public final class UriTemplate extends Object
Pure, dependency-free expander for URI Templates as defined by RFC 6570 (Levels 1–3).

A URI Template is a string containing literal text interspersed with brace-delimited {expression}s. Each expression names one or more template variables and, optionally, a leading operator that selects an expansion style. Expansion substitutes the variables with values taken from a caller-supplied map, percent-encoding each value according to the operator's allowed character set.

The following operators are supported (RFC 6570 §2.2, Appendix A): 

   {var}     Level 1  simple string expansion, percent-encode all but unreserved
   {+var}    Level 2  reserved expansion, leave reserved + unreserved unescaped
   {#var}    Level 2  fragment expansion, prefixes '#'
   {x,y}     Level 3  multiple variables joined by ','
   {.x}      Level 3  label expansion, prefixes and separates with '.'
   {/x}      Level 3  path-segment expansion, prefixes and separates with '/'
   {;x}      Level 3  path-style parameter expansion (name;name=value)
   {?x,y}    Level 3  form-style query, prefixes '?', separates with 'invalid input: '&'', name=value
   {invalid input: '&x'}      Level 3  form-style query continuation, prefixes 'invalid input: '&''

Value modifiers (RFC 6570 §2.4) are supported: the prefix modifier {var:3} takes the first three characters of a string value, and the explode modifier {var*} expands each member of a list or map individually.

A variable value may be a String (or any scalar rendered via toString()), a List (multi-valued list), or a Map (associative array). A variable that is absent, null, or an empty list/map is treated as undefined and omitted along with any separator it would have introduced (RFC 6570 §3.2.1).

The class performs no network or file I/O and is therefore fully offline-testable. Instances are immutable and thread-safe.
